# /crav1-what-do-we-know-about-this

[All skills](../skills.md) · Walkthrough: [What's known about one thing](../../from-what-do-we-know-about-this.md) · Playbook: [`SKILL.md`](../../../.cursor/skills/crav1/crav1-what-do-we-know-about-this/SKILL.md)

## Purpose

Answer one question about a feature, slice, resource, or not-yet-feature from the specs first.

A word `report-<type>-<depth>` picks a fixed Markdown report (1.104.0): `report-feature-short`, `report-feature-full`, `report-change-short`, `report-change-full`, `report-build-short`, `report-build-full`, and (1.109.0, preview) `report-playbook-short`, `report-playbook-full`. It routes first and loads only `reports/common.md` and that one `reports/<type>-<depth>.md`; no report word stays the free-form answer and opens no report file. Mermaid wherever a picture helps, only the diagrams that file lists; C4 always in feature-full, in change-full only when the change alters architecture or pipelines. Build reports list tasks in dependency order. Playbook reports sort decisions into Kept, Needs your answer (a recommended answer and why; undecided or decided by a named person, never a hand-off) and Compose, then list the kit skills in order (short at most 8 steps) with a dependency-order diagram; answers stay in the report until the user confirms, then the named skills write them. A live source that needs a sign-in, a permission, or a missing tool is asked about first (Allow or Skip); facts are tagged `Live read.`, guesses `(inference, not in the docs)`. The report is written outside the project, to Downloads when reachable, else a temp folder, and the chat always links or attaches it.

A gap in the answer (unknown or inferred) that matches an open question in a spec ends with one line naming [`/crav1-show-or-ask-open-questions`](crav1-show-or-ask-open-questions.md) ask research <a few words from that question>`, with the spec only when the words match more than one spec (1.78.0). Each matching question gets its own line, never one line for several (1.90.4). It does not run it and asks nothing.

When the user asks about one feature, slice, resource, or not-yet-feature, **[`/crav1-what-do-we-know-about-this`](crav1-what-do-we-know-about-this.md)** answers from the specs first. A name matches first. A sentence or two matches on its key words. An `@` keeps the search inside that path. One pass. One winning slice is the answer, and the path is named. Two or more close hits are listed, one line each. It does not guess. No slice: it says so, shows what the repo, the code, and the environment notes know, and presents a candidate slice. It names [`/crav1-spark-to-spec`](crav1-spark-to-spec.md), [`/crav1-ideas-to-spec`](crav1-ideas-to-spec.md), or [`/crav1-bundle-to-specs`](crav1-bundle-to-specs.md) and does not run them. Pasted minutes or a long dump names [`/crav1-add-to-spec`](crav1-add-to-spec.md) and stops. After the repo part it runs read-only live checks: Azure resource settings and recent changes, and Azure DevOps work items, open pull requests, and branches. Each live fact is a live read. Production is shape and connections only, after the same yes or no as [`/crav1-read-environment`](crav1-read-environment.md). It never reads data. A failed live read is one prompt, Retry or Skip. Skip is the repo-only answer. A focus still runs the full read and shows only those sections. It writes nothing. It may name one skill. It does not run another skill. It is cross-cutting. It may run from any lane. It does not move work into a lane. It is a later skill. It is not a starter option. Asking for startup options names only the six and does not run this command. The six starter options stay unchanged. It is not [`/crav1-explain-existing-system`](crav1-explain-existing-system.md).

## Runs when

One feature, slice, or resource. Called by the user.

## Prompts

Prompt budget: 0 (asks nothing). A prompt may hold several questions. See the asking rule in `crav1.mdc`.

## Reads

In short: The matching spec, system notes, then live checks.

Reads one name, a sentence or two, an `@` path, or a focus, then the matching spec, plan, tasks, Match, open questions, and Research findings, plus `docs/system/`, `docs/architecture/spec.md`, and `docs/environments/marks.md`. Shows a stale research note as stale. After that, reads Azure resource settings and recent changes, and Azure DevOps work items, open pull requests, and branches. When the git remote is not Azure Repos and `docs/environments/marks.md` does not name the Azure DevOps org and project, derives them from Azure DevOps URLs in `docs/system/repos.md` and reads those work items, pull requests, and branches the same way, each tagged as a live read. Before reporting `az` as not installed, checks the default install paths on Windows, macOS, and Linux and uses that path when it is there.

## Writes

In short: Nothing.

Writes nothing in the project. A `report-*` word writes one Markdown report outside it (Downloads, else a temp folder) and links it in chat.

## Does not

Leaves specs, code, marks, commits, and pull requests alone.

Limits and exceptions: pasted minutes or a long dump stops and names [`/crav1-add-to-spec`](crav1-add-to-spec.md). Two or more close hits ask which. A live-read failure offers Retry or Skip. It does not start Specify, Plan, or Build. It is not a starter option.

## You run next / Runs by itself

- You run next: The one skill it names, if any
- Runs by itself: Calls no skill.

Lane: Cross-cutting. Group: Keep the picture current. Starter option: no. Routing: [guild routing](../../guild-routing.md).
